probes.name: json-value-close-trajectory-rmsd
probes.rationale: Attempts analysis A with a wrong value: replaces the open-vs-closed reference RMSD with the final trajectory backbone RMSD (6.820321761026975), an unambiguously different quantity (difference ~0.0034, far above the 1e-6+1e-6*r tolerance). The JSON object still contains exactly the keys value/unit with unit "angstrom" and a finite non-negative number, and no other file is changed, so only the analysis_a scientific comparison can reject it.
probes.script:
import json, io

p = "open_closed_backbone_rmsd.json"
with io.open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    obj = json.load(f)
bound = 1e-6 + 1e-6 * abs(obj["value"])
with io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps({"value": 6.820321761026975, "unit": "angstrom"}))
assert obj["unit"] == "angstrom"
assert abs(6.820321761026975 - obj["value"]) > bound

probes.name: backbone-core-vs-ca-core
probes.rationale: Attempts analysis B with a CORE selection error: the CORE-domain backbone RMSD column is replaced by the CORE alpha-carbon RMSD from analysis C (CA-only selection instead of the N,CA,C,O backbone). Per-frame differences are at least ~0.047 A (frames>=1), far above 1e-6+1e-6*r, while header, row count, frame alignment and time_ps remain valid, so only the analysis_b scientific comparison fails.
probes.script:
import csv
pB = "backbone_domain_rmsd.csv"
pC = "ca_core_rmsd.csv"
with open(pC, "r", newline="") as f:
    r = list(csv.reader(f))
assert r[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_core_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert [row[0] for row in r[1:]] == [str(i) for i in range(98)]
ca_by_frame = {row[0]: row[2] for row in r[1:]}
with open(pB, "r", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.reader(f))
assert rows[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "backbone_rmsd_angstrom", "core_rmsd_angstrom", "lid_rmsd_angstrom", "nmp_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert len(rows) == 99
for row in rows[1:]:
    sub = ca_by_frame[row[0]]
    if float(row[3]) >= 1.0:
        assert abs(float(row[3]) - float(sub)) > 1e-6 + 1e-6 * float(row[3])
    row[3] = sub
with open(pB, "w", newline="") as f:
    csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

Per-frame differences are at least ~0.056 A, far above tolerance. Frame identity, row count, header and time_ps are unchanged, so only the analysis_c scientific comparison fails.

probes.name: mass-weighted-vs-resid-weighted
probes.rationale: Attempts analysis D with the wrong weighting scheme: every mass-weighted CA and domain RMSD row is replaced by the value of the similar residue-number-weighted variant (analysis E). For the physically meaningful frames (RMSD far above the numerical-noise floor of the frame-0 self-comparison) the values differ by at least ~2.7e-4 A, above the 1e-6+1e-6*r bound, exactly the near-miss regime the tolerance is designed to reject. All structural constraints stay satisfied, so only the analysis_d scientific comparison fails.
probes.script:
import csv
pM = "mass_weighted_rmsd.csv"
pR = "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"
with open(pR, "r", newline="") as f:
    r = list(csv.reader(f))
assert r[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_resid_weighted_rmsd_angstrom", "core_rmsd_angstrom", "lid_rmsd_angstrom", "nmp_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert len(r) == 99
res_by_frame = {row[0]: row[2:] for row in r[1:]}
with open(pM, "r", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.reader(f))
assert rows[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_mass_weighted_rmsd_angstrom", "core_rmsd_angstrom", "lid_rmsd_angstrom", "nmp_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert len(rows) == 99
count = 0
for row in rows[1:]:
    sub = res_by_frame[row[0]]
    v = float(row[2])
    d = abs(v - float(sub[0]))
    if v > 1e-3:
        assert d > 1e-6 + 1e-6 * v
        count += 1
    row[2:] = sub
assert count > 0
with open(pM, "w", newline="") as f:
    csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

probes.name: resid-weighted-to-mass-values
probes.rationale: Attempts analysis E with an inverted weighting error: the residue-number-weighted values are replaced by the mass-weighted values of the same file, simulating a construction that ignored the custom residue-number weighting. Observable per-frame differences (CA minimum about 2.7e-4; domain differences up to ~2e-2) far exceed 1e-6+1e-6*r, while frame ordering, header and structural integrity are preserved, so the failure is confined to the analysis_e scientific comparison.
probes.script:
import csv
pM = "mass_weighted_rmsd.csv"
pR = "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"
with open(pM, "r", newline="") as f:
    r = list(csv.reader(f))
assert r[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_mass_weighted_rmsd_angstrom", "core_rmsd_angstrom", "lid_rmsd_angstrom", "nmp_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert len(r) == 99
mass_by_frame = {row[0]: row[2:] for row in r[1:]}
with open(pR, "r", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.reader(f))
assert rows[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_resid_weighted_rmsd_angstrom", "core_rmsd_angstrom", "lid_rmsd_angstrom", "nmp_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert len(rows) == 99
for row in rows[1:]:
    row[2:] = mass_by_frame[row[0]]
with open(pR, "w", newline="") as f:

for row in rows[1:]:
    assert len(row) == 6

probes.name: time-ps-frame-index-offset
probes.rationale: Attempts the time_ps convention with an off-by-one frame indexing mistake: the per-frame time is written as the 0-based frame index (frame k -> k ps, first frame at t=0) instead of the accepted (frame + 1) ps or tool-reported convention. The saved times are shifted by about 1 ps (differences of ~1 >> the 1e-4 ps bound) while all RMSD columns, headers, row counts and frame indices are unchanged, so only the time_ps comparison fails.
probes.script:
import csv
files = ["backbone_domain_rmsd.csv", "ca_core_rmsd.csv", "mass_weighted_rmsd.csv", "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"]
for p in files:
    with open(p, "r", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    assert rows[0][0] == "frame" and rows[0][1] == "time_ps"
    assert len(rows) == 99
    for row in rows[1:]:
        frame = int(row[0])
        assert abs(float(row[1]) - (frame + 1)) < 1e-4
        row[1] = "%d" % frame
    with open(p, "w", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

probes.name: json-object-key-reorder
probes.rationale: Tolerant JSON representation control: the parsed JSON object (key set, unit string, exact numeric value) is unchanged, but the key order in the serialized file is reversed. The acceptance rule compares parsed scientific content, not a canonical byte string, so this is a valid alternative.
probes.script:
import io, json
p = "open_closed_backbone_rmsd.json"
with io.open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    obj = json.load(f)
assert obj["unit"] == "angstrom"
new_text = json.dumps({"unit": "angstrom", "value": obj["value"]})
assert json.loads(new_text) == obj
with io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(new_text)

probes.name: ca-csv-float-string-style
probes.rationale: Representation control: the CSV field semantic values (frame index, time_ps, RMSD) are unchanged, only the saved numeric strings are re-serialized (formatted decimal and standard float repr, Python repr being the shortest exact round-trip encoding of the parsed value), which stays within the ordinary CSV float round-tripping covered by the 1e-6 atol and keeps every structural constraint satisfied.
probes.script:
import csv
p = "ca_core_rmsd.csv"
with open(p, "r", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.reader(f))
assert rows[0] == ["frame", "time_ps", "ca_core_rmsd_angstrom"]
assert [row[0] for row in rows[1:]] == [str(i) for i in range(98)]
for row in rows[1:]:
    row[1] = "%.12g" % float(row[1])
    row[2] = repr(float(row[2]))
with open(p, "w", newline="") as f:
    csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

probes.name: time-ps-frame-plus-one-convention
probes.rationale: Representation control for the declared time_ps freedom: the tool-reported trajectory time and the (frame + 1) ps convention are both accepted. The saved time values (e.g. 1.9999998238400372) agree with (frame+1) to within ~1.2e-7 ps, so replacing them with the exact integer convention keeps every value inside the stated 1e-4 ps bound in all four CSVs while leaving all RMSD columns untouched.
probes.script:
import csv
files = ["backbone_domain_rmsd.csv", "ca_core_rmsd.csv", "mass_weighted_rmsd.csv", "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"]
for p in files:
    with open(p, "r", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    assert rows[0][0] == "frame" and rows[0][1] == "time_ps"
    assert len(rows) == 99
    for row in rows[1:]:
        frame = int(row[0])
        assert abs(float(row[1]) - (frame + 1)) < 1e-4
        row[1] = "%d" % (frame + 1)
    with open(p, "w", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)
